slides.heading: Calendar Matching
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Calendar Matching, a very hard arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Two people's meetings ("HH:MM" pairs) and daily bounds; return all free slots of at least `duration` minutes available to both.
Convert to minutes, merge busy intervals, invert.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Two people's meetings ("HH:MM" pairs) and daily bounds; return all free slots of at least duration minutes available to both. Convert to minutes, merge busy intervals, invert.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Merge both calendars, including bounds as meetings, then gaps of the right length are free slots.
slides.narration: Merge both calendars, including bounds as meetings, then gaps of the right length are free slots.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Check each minute of the day → O(1440)
Merge sorted busy intervals → O((n+m) log)
slides.narration: You could check every minute, but merging busy intervals is cleaner: add bounds as busy, sort, merge, and read off gaps.

slides.narration: Step by step. First, convert times to minutes. Second, add each person's bounds as blocked time. Third, sort and merge meetings. Fourth, return gaps at least duration long.
